A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAOT/VASOT research. All 15 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-alignment and action-segmentation experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measurements comparing the model size and training time of joint and separate models in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The FGW formulation, structural and temporal priors, virtual frames, encoder architecture and joint loss remain unchanged. Figure 2 clarifies existing encoder sharing. Stop-gradient operations remain depicted despite deletion of their explicit sentence in Section 3.2.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven datasets. Multi-action Penn Action alignment and per-video segmentation evaluation already appear in v1's appendices. The new efficiency comparison uses the existing Pouring and Desktop Assembly coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds HVQ to the full-dataset segmentation comparison on Breakfast and YouTube Instructions. Appendix A.7 also introduces a resource comparison against separate VAOT+ASOT models. Existing comparator memberships are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds evaluation by model size and training time for joint versus separate models, using ResNet-50 on Pouring and an MLP on Desktop Assembly with an Nvidia 3090Ti GPU. Existing benchmark protocols and the settings in Tables 4–5 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 adds an efficiency analysis testing whether joint modeling reduces storage and training time relative to separate models. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, retrieval examples, embedding visualizations and segmentation case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. The added comparisons introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All pre-existing table entries are unchanged. Table 3 adds HVQ's Breakfast MoF/F1 of 54.4/39.7 and YouTube Instructions 50.3/35.1; its Breakfast F1 exceeds VASOT's unchanged 39.0. A.7 adds VASOT versus VAOT+ASOT measurements: 108 versus 216 MB and 116 versus 162 minutes on Pouring; 287 versus 571 KB and 15 versus 21 minutes on Desktop Assembly.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, transport formulations, priors and losses in Equations 1–7, together with the solver complexity reasoning, are unchanged. Appendix A.7 supplies empirical resource measurements rather than new mathematical analysis or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty, performance and resource-saving claims. A repeated novelty sentence is removed from the introduction, but its substance remains elsewhere. The efficiency measurements support an existing claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes the specific suggestion of applying the harder alignment loss at a deeper layer; general deep supervision remains future work, and the conclusion adds complex loss weighting. The superiority interpretation now explicitly includes HVQ without acknowledging its higher Breakfast F1.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 newly identifies the Nvidia 3090Ti GPU and reports model sizes and training times for two encoder/dataset configurations. Existing implementation descriptions and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; no code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for HVQ, GradNorm and Kendall et al.'s uncertainty-based multi-task loss weighting. It removes Hyder et al.'s skeleton-heatmap segmentation and Khan et al.'s timestamp-supervised segmentation references. The main positioning relative to VAVA and ASOT remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits trim repeated statements and several pointers to supplementary material or cited details, revise future-work wording and extend the appendix roadmap for A.7. The abstract and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds shared-encoder labels and arrows; Figure 3's caption identifies the VAOT and VASOT panels. Table 3 gains the HVQ row and revised ranking emphasis. Table 8 moves from PDF page 11 to page 10, with associated reflow; existing plots and qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.7 supplies quantitative support for the previously unquantified storage and training-time claim, while HVQ makes the comparison more informative. These provide a modest overall gain, tempered by Section 4.3's now-incorrect claim of winning every metric: Table 3 correctly shows HVQ's Breakfast F1 of 39.7 above VASOT's 39.0.
